chapterTitle: Chapter 3: Synaptic Memoriam of a steel fossil shell
sceneTitle: Circa 2048 - Ghost’s in the sea of shells.
editorText:
<$Proj_H::3>Circa 2048 - Ghost’s in the sea of shells.<!$Proj_H::3>

“Back in the Wartimes this facility was a marker stone at the point of advancement for Mechanized and cyber warfare. It was crucial in bridging the link between the consciousness feedback loop of what is considered to make us human, into the shell of the machine. The founding ground of immortality some might say.”

TODO NOTE: Insert dramatic exit from John’s suit, he stumbles to the floor looking out over the sentient lying sleepless in eternity, and sheds a tear for those trapped here to lie in wake.

Although John’s team knew little about the sentient program. Their knowledge of the sentient project prior to John’s recent exposure to the Docs recording, was, that the countless carapaces scattered chaotically before them were no more than material amalgamations; Shai and Tao could feel from John’s energy that there was more going on here. That their captain had just witnessed something grim, unspeakable.

Something so terrible that it had seized him, stopped his unwavering momentum. His gaze was dead, eyes looking out across the valley, a still emptiness filled them as they gazed with no apparent direction. His shoulders slumped forward, his body rested lifelessly upon his knees. Then John felt something with of a firm presence in his empty space. Tex rested his hand on his shoulder, gripping him, gently squeezing with a light, friendly shove. “You good Cap?” Said Tex.

To the others this felt strange. Seeing a large, tough, man of few words now comforting their captain. This new version of Tex, the heartfelt teddy bear kind, was unusual. “We’re fish in a barrel here” said Tex with softly with concern. His eyes moved from John to the cliff tops where they remained vigilantly fixed. The alertness in his eyes didn’t match his charred wary armour, or the shortness in his breath as the words expired from his mouth. John’s heavy eye’s rose to meet Tex’s, still scanning the peaks above them.

Given Tex’s time in the 3rd war John trusted Tex’s intuition, or field sense as they termed it. “What the fuck are we waiting for” Tex pondered. He could feel what the captain had been overcome by, yet not quite piece everything together. after all his main purpose was to keep his team alive and he had little time for inquisition. “Yeeah, We’re standing out like Tex’s formiddable back hairs here” John pushed out in a soft yet cheerful undertone. Tex’s eyes defixed from the ridges and met with John’s “Hey! you must have a lot of free time to be eyeballing my back hair! ” John let out a playful smirk “I Agree with Tex, we should hug the cliff face, blend in a bit”.

 Tex did nothing, just uncomfortably stood there looking puzzled and confused. John Rose to his feet, then lifted his rifle's site to the saddle of the valley up ahead. “Ok team! keep your eyes on your sectors, use your suits to monitor the cliff ridge above our backs, let’s move!” Said John in a now more alert tone, infused with calm urgent authority. Like a trail of silent dark blue ants, John and his team moved delicately, yet decisively, keeping a strong pace as what remained of the evening light glimmered off their armoured suits, as an emerging rain spat lightly coating them in fine droplets of water. This had no effect on John’s team, other than the slight millisecond delay of their scan suites Geo map in their HUDS, due to the added sound filtering. Protectant suits were a site to behold, 2 generations ahead of their time. Their design had been curbed by AI creative suggestion, with the open node framework from all competitive businesses on the protectant ledger, the most reliable, state of the art sensor arrays had all emerged into one suit with one overarching purpose; The efficient insertion to diffuse conflicts, and preserve Life. stepping over the countless shells. Although lifeless, the shells emitted a dark presence, mangled steel, wire and silicon, in the violet purple evening sky. They were strewn randomly across the valley floor. From the rear of the machine's skulls, a deep huss blue glowed silently. They weren't human corpses, but they felt human. Tau imagined a sea of glow worms dancing elegantly between stars inside the machine’s heads. Carefully they walked, trying not to disturb the sea of blue souls, the sea of the sentient dead. While their power cores had diminished and been discharged, yet the gelatinous mass which held their computer network absorbed the suns rays through the day, emitting a calming bioluminescence in the evening, dimly lighting the valley floor as a dark shade blanketed across the valley in the evening. John thought to himself “There is still hope for these Sentients, they fight against the darkness, even lying peacefully in their graves”

John strategically placed each step over the cold carapaces. Only small amounts of glimmering light penetrated through the thick fog which opened up usually at corners and wind pockets that had pushed away fog through the winding valley. John was the first to reach the cliff face. He shifted his back to the wall, then placed his hand on Tao’s shoulder looking back he could see Shai followed by Tex falling into line along the cliff face behind them.

“Get the Peregrine’s up, we need two scans in either direction for any cavities or caverns, We need to get out of site” Said John with a cool calmness. still hugging the cliff face with his team like a snake sheltering from light.

“I have two Peregrine’s charged and ready to for launch” Tao was confidently tapping away on her terminal, Then she moved her palm bac k to her rifles grip. Momentarily after she shouldered her rifle, two bulbous looking bumps on the back of Tao’s suit ejected slightly as circular ports recessed into her suit forming an annex around what looked like now a nose conned mushroom Two narrow drones shot out almost vertically but at a slight angle like missiles, with small blue plumes shooting out from their bases, once they reached above the cliff’s ridge line, two gliding wings springed out from both of them, as they darted off in opposite directions scanning the valley as they whisped by.

Tex was now becoming inpatient. “Link up!” shot Tex, while him and Shai covered the rear, Tao and John covered the front. Immediately Tao rested her rifle on John’s shoulder, as did Shai’s on Tex’s. within milliseconds of the other, a magnetic hum and clamp sound silently let out, as Tao and Shai’s rifles magnetically coupled to John’s and Tex’s shoulder. Each of the girl's free hand’s shifted to the other shoulder for support and in doing so they had turned on the magnetic couple on their rifles through an inbuilt inductive circuit in each shoulder of the protective suit. All they had to do was remove their free hand from their team mates shoulder, and the mounting device on their rifles which sat atop an inbuilt gimbal for manoeuvrability disengaged. releasing the electromagnets charge disengaging the rifle from it’s mount coupling.

John bobbed his had to the right drawing Tao’s attention. “How’re the peregrines techy?”. Before Tao could speak a word the mapped out geometry of the valley was shot up in John’s HUD. Took aback john stumbled back, knocking into the cliff face off centred. He wasn’t expecting such a sudden interface into Tao’s feed. out of no-where a cheery voice chimed in “I took the honour of pre-compiling the report for you Cap!”. Tao looked over to John for a brief second, slightly lowering her weapons site, she shrugged her shoulders. “It looks like you weren’t the only one who got an upgrade” confused by what had just transpired, the others could hear a slight annoyance in Tao’s voice as she tried to peace together how Kitten had access to their interfaces. “Fucking Bitch, you eclipsed me!” Tao contained her thoughts, and let Kitten continue. After all it wasn’t the time for chit chat. “” It appears there are no cavities to be found captain, in either direction for 4 miles”. John let out an unimpressed sigh, looking down at his feet shaking his head slowly. He knew what would happen to his team if they didn’t find shelter soon. “Although Captain, I did detect an anomaly on the scan within 700 feet of our location!, and it isn’t us, both drone’s systems are operating at 100%” Kitten paused, as though waiting for a response, instead the moment “anomaly” Tao had begun frantically tapping away at her wrist terminal like a mad scientist on the verge of a breakthrough. “Aaah captain!” Tao was uneasy in her assumption, you could hear her voice breaking apart, but she continued anyway, flicking on her wrist terminal in the direction of John as though she was throwing her terminals view to his Helmet HUD. John could now see two 3D Model charts of an area up ahead in the valley. “What your viewing is the anomaly location!” chimed Kitten, “not now you AI bitch, you’re stealing my light” Thought Tao but she remained quiet giving John a moment. John could see two 3D scans, one unfazed John, the other on the right however, presented scattered dots of 3D scan points, which made up what looked like the body of a speckled worm, winding deep within the mountain face. Tao continued “That anomaly that Kitten picked up on.. I ran a signal transform from depth spikes in the cliff face from the peregrine” John could now see that the left scan wasn’t quite right, with something that looked like hairlines breaching into the cliff, He gathered these were the impulse spikes Tao was talking about. “It seems that some new light emission technology is being used to project an image over an existing cavity in the rock face, however faint.. there were also some spikes not visible to the human eye that were picked up as the anomaly on our original scans. From these spikes I was able to smooth out a transform signal and remove the blocking sound. It seems a sound device is being used to block any incoming echo location scans, nothing showed up on visual, Lidar or Sound, other than the spikes of course, but I believe these are just a flaw in the design.. maybe..” John cut Tao off with a reserved kindness in his tone. “That’s great Tao, but get to the point”. Tao stood up from her crouched position, easing her shoulders back as she did now confident in what she was seeing “There’s a tunnel up ahead cap, I’m not sure how deep, but it’s worth checking out!”

John stood up shouldering his rifle and stretching his legs slightly as he raised it. “Alright, Excellent work Tao. Let’s check it out, but keep in mind, whatever was cloaking that cavity isn’t our tech. We don’t know what’s waiting for us on the other side”. John was assertive in his response. “Keep your sector work tidy and check your angles.. Tao when we get close I want you to pilot a drone in, how many do we have left?” “1 captain, I have a beetle,” said Tao. The beetle was a more nimble drone, with a circular design, meant for  Close Quarter Combat environment scans, and most protectant suit’s came with one particularly special insertion teams. “Ok.. big guy! you’re up back ” Tex shouldered his Sherpa then fell in line behind the others. Being so broad across the shoulders it was too hard to see past the towering mass of muscle meat, bone and armour, little own keep pace with his steps which felt like small leaps for the others. He was big, but he was still fast in his uncommonly large protectant suit. “You bet cap” Tex shot back, “I got the 6” He wasn’t so enthusiastic about the last part, but he understood why. “Let’s run this smooth, don’t get ahead of yourselves, and make sure you have your system set to cold-blooded” said John. He knew now that shelter was not far off, and any excessive use of radar, might only now increase their chances of being detected.

Like a snake protecting it’s fragile body, avoiding a ferocious honey badgers scent, Walker and his team continued deeper downhill into the valley. This technique was common in stealth operations, and all too familiar to Tex. Tex had served prior to the final war. He knew how to move undetected, yet times were different.

Newer technology on LRD’s had focused long range scanning capabilities. They could detect even smaller protrusions across a face with inbuilt geographical training to make out unusual structures or possible lifeforms. A team of well equipped protectants in the middle of a Valley would start sending off alarm bells on it’s long range scanners, without even mentioning the profound presence of electrical activity within their kits. The ream really did embody the presence of a snake,  silent, cold and uniform in their movement. Tao’s suit was equipped with subsonic receivers. Metaphorically speaking she was the belly, always listening, John the eye’s and tongue with a taste for field sense, Shai the nervous system always watching over all it’s moving parts and internal organs. And Tex the hardened scales handling anything too big that might come there way. The last resort, like a leashed pit bull waiting to be let loose, yet cool and calm as houses under walker’s command. They’d made a good steady pace about 90% of the way when Tao raised her right forearm with a closed fist, giving the signal to the others to stop. In doing so Tao’s suit’s inbuilt inertia sensors had already detected her pose, and sent a short faint beeping sound to her squad-mates earpieces. In unison they all stopped, still, quiet. There was no need for verbal activity, they remained silent.

Protectant suits had been uniquely designed  to improve communications universally among teams, enabling them to know what their squad-mates were doing without having to move their eyes from their rifles' sites. Not only did John and his team move seamlessly together, but watching them it felt as though they were one body, moving together with little effort. Protectant suits gave the users the ability to draw their squad-mates attention  purely off movement and sign signals, to pass sound coded voice comm’s thoughtlessly in unison. Afterall, the sound of a small microphone in a protectants ear was far less detectable than that of yelled commands. Even with the sound dampening properties of the helmets, their voices could still be slightly heard. In extreme situations, hand signals were just as efficient.

Tao flicked her wrist terminal, sending her HUD view to John once again. John could see on his HUD a 3D rotating model of a long range drone, an amber alert could be seen accompanying sound frequencies matching that of the LRD engines, “LRD signature detected 20 miles out”. “For now we are safe” Said Tao softly, Just above a whisper. John could hear the relief in her voice. “At it’s current speed it will be on us in 3 minutes, the precision of that things scanners a minute out is almost seamless, the cliff mesh won’t be enough to conceal us past 2 minutes, then our cover is blown” Tex intervened calmly, meeting Tao’s tone, yet firmly.  John observed tex looking at his suit’s rear view in his HUD trying to think of something, anything “Kitten! can you copy the same tech of the anomaly we detected earlier and..” Tao cut John off “Convert our transmitters to mimic the same geo scan blocking technology that was present at the anomaly!” she’d finished John’s sentence for him, with some improvisation and youthful enthusiasm. “Such a signal would require a distributed source to smooth out the power draw and any bumps on the system. I’ve sent the configuration to your HUDS'' chimed kitten.

A small window shot up from kittens' interface in their HUDS, displaying a topical view of the team spread out against the cliff's face, recessed into a small cavity, just not big enough to  conceal them fully, given the size of their suits combined. They could see their own names next to pin nodes, indicating a power link up formation kitten had determined.  Tex had began unscrewing a small circular cover just over an inch in diameter on his lower right abdomen.  with his free hand, still holding his rifle to his eye, covering his sector. The cover now collapsed outwards, hanging from a small hinge that had been recessed into the suit. The whole manoeuvre  was silent. “Power port open” Kitten chirped. Tex pressed a small stainless steel ring face, recessed in the port. A small cylindrical power connection device protruded from his suit’s power port, just enough so that he could grab it. John firmly gripping the connector with his free hand pulled the excess cable out from his suit simultaneously. Tex placed his rifle on his back, magnetic couples locked in securing it in place with a crisp click. He laid his hand on Shai’s shoulder pulling her into him while he inserted the connection into her suit’s power inlet at the lower rear of her abdomen.“link established, power draw capacity increased by 50%”, Kitten announced the moment Tex was firmly connected, as the others linked in to one another the general AI continued. “draw capability increased by 100%, 150%, 200%”.

Tao frantically looked over at Tex “10 seconds till we are in the LRD’s detection range!, 9.. 8.. 7..” Tao counted down with a calm urgency, going silent at five seconds. There was a sense of professionalism in her tone, she knew she had a job to do, they all did, so she did her best to create fluidity in the team's actions. A bead of sweat trickled down along Shai’s forehead stinging her eye, she leaned forward in her helmet wiping the assault of beads away with her helmet liner as she let out a short sigh. John was looking back at Tex, he pointed his fingers like a pistol in signing, then clenched his fist, exploding his fingers outwards. “Arm Railstorm '' chimed Kitten after detecting John's sign language. The countdown displayed in the HUD, letting out a soft digital bleep with each passing second. Tex dismounted the Railstorm from the lower rear of his suit, mounting it on his already towering shoulders, the HUD count still continuing.. ‘Three, Two’, “Hard Mesh Loading” Chirped kitten, unphased by the gravity of her surroundings. The Hard light mesh Kitten had termed it, was nowhere to be seen.  John looked back at Tao waiting in anticipation, rifle at the ready, the others shuffled closer in against the cliff to try and conceal their suit geometry, doubtful this “Mesh” would even work. “Get ready to..” “Hard Mesh Up!” Kitten chirped, interrupting Tao. Tao gave a big inhale then let out a sigh of relief. Shai’s eyes were now wide open, entranced by the beauty of what was unfolding before their eyes. Tex looked around confused, slightly in shock.

What seemed like an unravelling glimmering blanket comprised of shards of light protruding towards them, smooth on the outside draped down from an upward channel of energy which shout out from all four of their suit’s communications modules, linking up at the apex of the internally sparkling dome. Waves rippled across the inside of the blanket, like wind against a curtain. The shards retract and extrude, maintaining what seemed from looking outwards like an almost transparent shell of an imagined cliff face that they could see, but wasn’t actually there. John and his team rose from their kneeling positions, their arms slack at their sides, loosely gripping their rifles. Tex’s still holstered at the ready, although the big man nonetheless looked on, fixated in a trance for seconds that felt like days gazing through the blanket of spectral light.  Suddenly like a bucket of ice cold water had been thrown over their heads, John Tex and Shai shuffled back against the cliff face once more, awakening from what felt like a dream, they kneeled back down shouldering their rifles. Tex redeployed his Railstorm, his finger resting delicately on the trigger. In the distance the whirl of large drone turbines echoed through the valley. Tao confirmed the approaching sound with an alarm on her wrist  “It’s heading our way but it’s taking it’s time! it seems to be scraping the valley just above the peaks following the ridge line, 40 meters out”

Seconds passed by silently  “Where is this fucking thing” Tex whispered delicately, Tao perplexed still standing, punched her wrist panel responding calmly, “It should be on top of us now”. Something was approaching fast, but none of them could see it, “LRD approaching” flashed red, accompanied by a rapidly decreasing countdown displaying the drones distance from their location. For a brief pause the countdown stopped. “Proximity warning 10 meters.. Proximity warning 10 meters” pulsed persistently.

Enshrouded in a cloak of glimmering light, John and his team didn’t feel safe, or embraced, yet a grim feeling of insecurity lurked as the proximity counter pulsed away. Thoughts of the drones whereabouts quashed now any admiration of the cloaking mesh. They sat anxiously waiting; the flickering proximity warning in their HUDS remained fixed at ten meters. “Are we being targeted for Fuck Sake”, Thought John, barely able to scan the sky overhead past the veil of shimmering light. All was quiet for a brief moment, and then it wasn’t. A thunderous roar shook the walls of the mountain steeps, sending rubble falling all around. Stones and granite showered through the light mesh sending ripples in their wake distorting the sphere's cloak ever so lightly. The Long Range drone had been transgressing the peak ridges hugging the winding cliff face while throwing off their distance sensors. Now it was entering their valley, descending straight onto of them.

The Engine signature of the LRD was now so strong, Tao’s HUD readout displayed 100% confirmation on the engine signature. “Protectant LRD sparrow class” whispered Tao, “Fuck, just what we need” thought John. No more than a second had passed before a large shadow passed over them. The footprint slightly larger than a small car homed in directly above them turning to that of a minibus. emerging from the fog drawing a wake of waves that rippled behind it’s wake. The drone hovered intimidatingly, armed with an array of rail guns, the armour piercing type, ballistic missiles and targeted EMP cannons along its sides. What remained of the evening sun's blue light somehow penetrated the fog, flickered off the pilot-less cockpit strewn with sensor arrays and telemetry. John could see its outline illuminated clear as day through his own eyes. Energy pulsed through its parts like blood through veins, where the others squinted trying to glean their kill shots amongst the mass of steel and technology. It was hard as the underbelly only revealed so much in the evening light, and their thermal sensors only revealed minor details of the drones underbelly.

“Fuck”, Tex let out gently.. The drone pivoted on one location scanning left to right. It's thrusters angling opposite directions throwing a wave of heated dust in their direction. Then it hopped strafing to the left and began pivoting again, but still in their direction as if it knew something was off, like it could smell them. With each shift of the drone Tex’s trigger finger twitched a little as he compensated the weight of the Railstorm to track the sparrows movements. Then it stopped for a second. A bead of sweat ran over the protruded veins on Tex’s forehead, then down into his eye with a stinging sensation. Yet he seemed unmoved by it focused determined to keep the sparrow in the Railstorms targeting reticle. The drone began to pivot once more horizontally but this time much slower. It felt timeless. John raised his hand with his palm open, but still. “Hold fire” displayed across his team’s HUDS. The drone still scanning slowly stopped, then let out a loud deafening sound, like that of a mechanical trumpet deep but with resonating hums, seeming almost like an echo-location scan. The shimmering blanket strewn around them seemed to ripple internally, almost as if to deflect any sound coming in. Then there was silence.

The engines of the sparrow spun up, the heat on the ground intensified as a whirlwind of dust stirred, the plume of the sparrow’s thrusters shifted from a blue to a deep violet as it ascended rapidly back up the cliff face, a shower of aggregates and stone toppled to the valley floor once again in its wake. “ I don’t believe what I just witnessed but it fucking worked! ” Tao celebrated internally, excited for the implications this meant for her team. She felt at peace, secure. “Tao, any chance that thing picks up on anomalies similar to the tech we Just copied?” John wasn’t yet convinced they were clear just yet. “It looks like the Tectonic plate shifts in the region may have thrown off the original mesh scan we picked up earlier Cap” said Tao, “We don’t seem to be exhibiting any spikes, other than the curtain breaks from the falling debris. I think we’re in the clear for now”.

Tex lowered the Railstorm, letting out a deep sigh of relief. “Not sure how much longer I could have held target lock there, that was.. Tense” John looked over his shoulder back at Tex and nodded as if to say thanks for having our back. “Kitten” Shot John. “We clear?”, “Copy Captain” Kitten shot back, “And what about that anomaly we detected up ahead?, any chance of that thing coming back to investigate? I’d rather skip the reunion”, “Given the circumstances captain I’m not sure we have any other options, but we can possibly re-mesh the cloaking field once we get to it’s location!”. As soon as Kitten got her last words out, John rose to his feet with intent shouldering his rifle as though nothing had just occurred. The others still wondering how they’s managed to still be breathing this far. “I’m certainly not waiting for that drone to come back around” Tex closed his statement off with the sound of a a high explosive round chambering in his rifle.

“Powering down hard-light mesh” Kitten let out as the other’s shouldered and checked their rifles. The flickering curtain of light diminished, lifting from the ground up around them retracting into nothing, letting in the kiss of the evening starlight which now painted the valley a pale blue before them. The subtle humm of their suit’s hydrogen packs eased to silence, all within the grasp of a second, the light mesh was gone and the team was geared and ready to move. That’s all they needed. Without a word John began moving towards the anomalies marker on his HUD. The others tightly behind him lightly brushing the cliff face, not touching but ever so carefully hugging.

He knew what would happen to his team if they didn’t find shelter soon. “Although Captain, I did detect an anomaly on the scan within 700 feet of our location!, and it isn’t us, both drone’s systems are operating at 100%” Kitten paused, as though waiting for a response, instead the moment “anomaly” Tao had begun frantically tapping away at her wrist terminal like a mad scientist on the verge of a breakthrough. “Aaah captain!” Tao was uneasy in her assumption, you could hear her voice breaking apart, but she continued anyway, flicking on her wrist terminal in the direction of John as though she was throwing her terminals view to his Helmet HUD. John could now see two 3D Model charts of an area up ahead in the valley. “What your viewing is the anomaly location!” chimed Kitten, “not now you AI bitch, you’re stealing my light” Thought Tao but she remained quiet giving John a moment. John could see two 3D scans, one unfazed John, the other on the right however, presented scattered dots of 3D scan points, which made up what looked like the body of a speckled worm, winding deep within the mountain face. Tao continued “That anomaly that Kitten picked up on.. I ran a signal transform from depth spikes in the cliff face from the peregrine” John could now see that the left scan wasn’t quite right, with something that looked like hairlines breaching into the cliff, He gathered these were the impulse spikes Tao was talking about. “It seems that some new light emission technology is being used to project an image over an existing cavity in the rock face, however faint.. there were also some spikes not visible to the human eye that were picked up as the anomaly on our original scans. From these spikes I was able to smooth out a transform signal and remove the blocking sound. It seems a sound device is being used to block any incoming echo location scans, nothing showed up on visual, Lidar or Sound, other than the spikes of course, but I believe these are just a flaw in the design.. maybe..” John cut Tao off with a reserved kindness in his tone. “That’s great Tao, but get to the point”. Tao stood up from her crouched position, easing her shoulders back as she did now confident in what she was seeing “There’s a tunnel up ahead cap, I’m not sure how deep, but it’s worth checking out!”

John stood up shouldering his rifle and stretching his legs slightly as he raised it. “Alright, Excellent work Tao. Let’s check it out, but keep in mind, whatever was cloaking that cavity isn’t our tech. We don’t know what’s waiting for us on the other side”. John was assertive in his response. “Keep your sector work tidy and check your angles.. Tao when we get close I want you to pilot a drone in, how many do we have left?” “1 captain, I have a beetle,” said Tao. The beetle was a more nimble drone, with a circular design, meant for  Close Quarter Combat environment scans, and most protectant suit’s came with one particularly special insertion teams. “Ok.. big guy! you’re up back ” Tex shouldered his Sherpa then fell in line behind the others. Being so broad across the shoulders it was too hard to see past the towering mass of muscle meat, bone and armour, little own keep pace with his steps which felt like small leaps for the others. He was big, but he was still fast in his uncommonly large protectant suit. “You bet cap” Tex shot back, “I got the 6” He wasn’t so enthusiastic about the last part, but he understood why. “Let’s run this smooth, don’t get ahead of yourselves, and make sure you have your system set to cold-blooded” said John. He knew now that shelter was not far off, and any excessive use of radar, might only now increase their chances of being detected.

Like a snake protecting it’s fragile body, avoiding a ferocious honey badgers scent, Walker and his team continued deeper downhill into the valley. This technique was common in stealth operations, and all too familiar to Tex. Tex had served prior to the final war. He knew how to move undetected, yet times were different.

Newer technology on LRD’s had focused long range scanning capabilities. They could detect even smaller protrusions across a face with inbuilt geographical training to make out unusual structures or possible lifeforms. A team of well equipped protectants in the middle of a Valley would start sending off alarm bells on it’s long range scanners, without even mentioning the profound presence of electrical activity within their kits. The ream really did embody the presence of a snake,  silent, cold and uniform in their movement. Tao’s suit was equipped with subsonic receivers. Metaphorically speaking she was the belly, always listening, John the eye’s and tongue with a taste for field sense, Shai the nervous system always watching over all it’s moving parts and internal organs. And Tex the hardened scales handling anything too big that might come there way. The last resort, like a leashed pit bull waiting to be let loose, yet cool and calm as houses under walker’s command. They’d made a good steady pace about 90% of the way when Tao raised her right forearm with a closed fist, giving the signal to the others to stop. In doing so Tao’s suit’s inbuilt inertia sensors had already detected her pose, and sent a short faint beeping sound to her squad-mates earpieces. In unison they all stopped, still, quiet. There was no need for verbal activity, they remained silent.

Protectant suits had been uniquely designed  to improve communications universally among teams, enabling them to know what their squad-mates were doing without having to move their eyes from their rifles' sites. Not only did John and his team move seamlessly together, but watching them it felt as though they were one body, moving together with little effort. Protectant suits gave the users the ability to draw their squad-mates attention  purely off movement and sign signals, to pass sound coded voice comm’s thoughtlessly in unison. Afterall, the sound of a small microphone in a protectants ear was far less detectable than that of yelled commands. Even with the sound dampening properties of the helmets, their voices could still be slightly heard. In extreme situations, hand signals were just as efficient.

Tao flicked her wrist terminal, sending her HUD view to John once again. John could see on his HUD a 3D rotating model of a long range drone, an amber alert could be seen accompanying sound frequencies matching that of the LRD engines, “LRD signature detected 20 miles out”. “For now we are safe” Said Tao softly, Just above a whisper. John could hear the relief in her voice. “At it’s current speed it will be on us in 3 minutes, the precision of that things scanners a minute out is almost seamless, the cliff mesh won’t be enough to conceal us past 2 minutes, then our cover is blown” Tex intervened calmly, meeting Tao’s tone, yet firmly.  John observed tex looking at his suit’s rear view in his HUD trying to think of something, anything “Kitten! can you copy the same tech of the anomaly we detected earlier and..” Tao cut John off “Convert our transmitters to mimic the same geo scan blocking technology that was present at the anomaly!” she’d finished John’s sentence for him, with some improvisation and youthful enthusiasm. “Such a signal would require a distributed source to smooth out the power draw and any bumps on the system. I’ve sent the configuration to your HUDS'' chimed kitten.

A small window shot up from kittens' interface in their HUDS, displaying a topical view of the team spread out against the cliff's face, recessed into a small cavity, just not big enough to  conceal them fully, given the size of their suits combined. They could see their own names next to pin nodes, indicating a power link up formation kitten had determined.  Tex had began unscrewing a small circular cover just over an inch in diameter on his lower right abdomen.  with his free hand, still holding his rifle to his eye, covering his sector. The cover now collapsed outwards, hanging from a small hinge that had been recessed into the suit. The whole manoeuvre  was silent. “Power port open” Kitten chirped. Tex pressed a small stainless steel ring face, recessed in the port. A small cylindrical power connection device protruded from his suit’s power port, just enough so that he could grab it. John firmly gripping the connector with his free hand pulled the excess cable out from his suit simultaneously. Tex placed his rifle on his back, magnetic couples locked in securing it in place with a crisp click. He laid his hand on Shai’s shoulder pulling her into him while he inserted the connection into her suit’s power inlet at the lower rear of her abdomen.“link established, power draw capacity increased by 50%”, Kitten announced the moment Tex was firmly connected, as the others linked in to one another the general AI continued. “draw capability increased by 100%, 150%, 200%”.

Tao frantically looked over at Tex “10 seconds till we are in the LRD’s detection range!, 9.. 8.. 7..” Tao counted down with a calm urgency, going silent at five seconds. There was a sense of professionalism in her tone, she knew she had a job to do, they all did, so she did her best to create fluidity in the team's actions. A bead of sweat trickled down along Shai’s forehead stinging her eye, she leaned forward in her helmet wiping the assault of beads away with her helmet liner as she let out a short sigh. John was looking back at Tex, he pointed his fingers like a pistol in signing, then clenched his fist, exploding his fingers outwards. “Arm Railstorm '' chimed Kitten after detecting John's sign language. The countdown displayed in the HUD, letting out a soft digital bleep with each passing second. Tex dismounted the Railstorm from the lower rear of his suit, mounting it on his already towering shoulders, the HUD count still continuing.. ‘Three, Two’, “Hard Mesh Loading” Chirped kitten, unphased by the gravity of her surroundings. The Hard light mesh Kitten had termed it, was nowhere to be seen.  John looked back at Tao waiting in anticipation, rifle at the ready, the others shuffled closer in against the cliff to try and conceal their suit geometry, doubtful this “Mesh” would even work. “Get ready to..” “Hard Mesh Up!” Kitten chirped, interrupting Tao. Tao gave a big inhale then let out a sigh of relief. Shai’s eyes were now wide open, entranced by the beauty of what was unfolding before their eyes. Tex looked around confused, slightly in shock.

What seemed like an unravelling glimmering blanket comprised of shards of light protruding towards them, smooth on the outside draped down from an upward channel of energy which shout out from all four of their suit’s communications modules, linking up at the apex of the internally sparkling dome. Waves rippled across the inside of the blanket, like wind against a curtain. The shards retract and extrude, maintaining what seemed from looking outwards like an almost transparent shell of an imagined cliff face that they could see, but wasn’t actually there. John and his team rose from their kneeling positions, their arms slack at their sides, loosely gripping their rifles. Tex’s still holstered at the ready, although the big man nonetheless looked on, fixated in a trance for seconds that felt like days gazing through the blanket of spectral light.  Suddenly like a bucket of ice cold water had been thrown over their heads, John Tex and Shai shuffled back against the cliff face once more, awakening from what felt like a dream, they kneeled back down shouldering their rifles. Tex redeployed his Railstorm, his finger resting delicately on the trigger. In the distance the whirl of large drone turbines echoed through the valley. Tao confirmed the approaching sound with an alarm on her wrist  “It’s heading our way but it’s taking it’s time! it seems to be scraping the valley just above the peaks following the ridge line, 40 meters out”

Seconds passed by silently  “Where is this fucking thing” Tex whispered delicately, Tao perplexed still standing, punched her wrist panel responding calmly, “It should be on top of us now”. Something was approaching fast, but none of them could see it, “LRD approaching” flashed red, accompanied by a rapidly decreasing countdown displaying the drones distance from their location. For a brief pause the countdown stopped. “Proximity warning 10 meters.. Proximity warning 10 meters” pulsed persistently.

Enshrouded in a cloak of glimmering light, John and his team didn’t feel safe, or embraced, yet a grim feeling of insecurity lurked as the proximity counter pulsed away. Thoughts of the drones whereabouts quashed now any admiration of the cloaking mesh. They sat anxiously waiting; the flickering proximity warning in their HUDS remained fixed at ten meters. “Are we being targeted for Fuck Sake”, Thought John, barely able to scan the sky overhead past the veil of shimmering light. All was quiet for a brief moment, and then it wasn’t. A thunderous roar shook the walls of the mountain steeps, sending rubble falling all around. Stones and granite showered through the light mesh sending ripples in their wake distorting the sphere's cloak ever so lightly. The Long Range drone had been transgressing the peak ridges hugging the winding cliff face while throwing off their distance sensors. Now it was entering their valley, descending straight onto of them.

The Engine signature of the LRD was now so strong, Tao’s HUD readout displayed 100% confirmation on the engine signature. “Protectant LRD sparrow class” whispered Tao, “Fuck, just what we need” thought John. No more than a second had passed before a large shadow passed over them. The footprint slightly larger than a small car homed in directly above them turning to that of a minibus. emerging from the fog drawing a wake of waves that rippled behind it’s wake. The drone hovered intimidatingly, armed with an array of rail guns, the armour piercing type, ballistic missiles and targeted EMP cannons along its sides. What remained of the evening sun's blue light somehow penetrated the fog, flickered off the pilot-less cockpit strewn with sensor arrays and telemetry. John could see its outline illuminated clear as day through his own eyes. Energy pulsed through its parts like blood through veins, where the others squinted trying to glean their kill shots amongst the mass of steel and technology. It was hard as the underbelly only revealed so much in the evening light, and their thermal sensors only revealed minor details of the drones underbelly.

“Fuck”, Tex let out gently.. The drone pivoted on one location scanning left to right. It's thrusters angling opposite directions throwing a wave of heated dust in their direction. Then it hopped strafing to the left and began pivoting again, but still in their direction as if it knew something was off, like it could smell them. With each shift of the drone Tex’s trigger finger twitched a little as he compensated the weight of the Railstorm to track the sparrows movements. Then it stopped for a second. A bead of sweat ran over the protruded veins on Tex’s forehead, then down into his eye with a stinging sensation. Yet he seemed unmoved by it focused determined to keep the sparrow in the Railstorms targeting reticle. The drone began to pivot once more horizontally but this time much slower. It felt timeless. John raised his hand with his palm open, but still. “Hold fire” displayed across his team’s HUDS. The drone still scanning slowly stopped, then let out a loud deafening sound, like that of a mechanical trumpet deep but with resonating hums, seeming almost like an echo-location scan. The shimmering blanket strewn around them seemed to ripple internally, almost as if to deflect any sound coming in. Then there was silence.

The engines of the sparrow spun up, the heat on the ground intensified as a whirlwind of dust stirred, the plume of the sparrow’s thrusters shifted from a blue to a deep violet as it ascended rapidly back up the cliff face, a shower of aggregates and stone toppled to the valley floor once again in its wake. “ I don’t believe what I just witnessed but it fucking worked! ” Tao celebrated internally, excited for the implications this meant for her team. She felt at peace, secure. “Tao, any chance that thing picks up on anomalies similar to the tech we Just copied?” John wasn’t yet convinced they were clear just yet. “It looks like the Tectonic plate shifts in the region may have thrown off the original mesh scan we picked up earlier Cap” said Tao, “We don’t seem to be exhibiting any spikes, other than the curtain breaks from the falling debris. I think we’re in the clear for now”.

Tex lowered the Railstorm, letting out a deep sigh of relief. “Not sure how much longer I could have held target lock there, that was.. Tense” John looked over his shoulder back at Tex and nodded as if to say thanks for having our back. “Kitten” Shot John. “We clear?”, “Copy Captain” Kitten shot back, “And what about that anomaly we detected up ahead?, any chance of that thing coming back to investigate? I’d rather skip the reunion”, “Given the circumstances captain I’m not sure we have any other options, but we can possibly re-mesh the cloaking field once we get to it’s location!”. As soon as Kitten got her last words out, John rose to his feet with intent shouldering his rifle as though nothing had just occurred. The others still wondering how they’s managed to still be breathing this far. “I’m certainly not waiting for that drone to come back around” Tex closed his statement off with the sound of a a high explosive round chambering in his rifle.

“Powering down hard-light mesh” Kitten let out as the other’s shouldered and checked their rifles. The flickering curtain of light diminished, lifting from the ground up around them retracting into nothing, letting in the kiss of the evening starlight which now painted the valley a pale blue before them. The subtle humm of their suit’s hydrogen packs eased to silence, all within the grasp of a second, the light mesh was gone and the team was geared and ready to move. That’s all they needed. Without a word John began moving towards the anomalies marker on his HUD. The others tightly behind him lightly brushing the cliff face, not touching but ever so carefully hugging.
